\chapter{Programs — Runs Stay In Limits}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Programs.Light.RunsStayInLimits
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Programs.Light.RunsStayInLimits}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Bound under a function update]
\lean{Light.abs_update_le}
\label{Light.abs_update_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ and $B,v\in\mathbb Z$. If $|f(y)|\le B$ for every
$y\in\mathbb N$ and $|v|\le B$, then replacing the value of $f$ at any $x\in\mathbb N$
by $v$ leaves every value bounded in absolute value by $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on safe expression values]
\lean{Light.Expr.abs_val_le}
\label{Light.Expr.abs_val_le}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Expr, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.val, Light.State, Light.State.Bounded}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\sigma$ be a state whose location and memory values all have absolute value at most
the word limit. Then every expression $e$ that is safe in $\sigma$ has value satisfying
$|e(\sigma)|\le$ the word limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded state from a frame]
\lean{Light.bounded_frame}
\label{Light.bounded_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Light.AbsLe.abs_getD_le, Light.State.Bounded, Light.frame}
\difficulty{1}
Let the word bound be $W$, let $\text{args}$ be a finite list of integers, and let
$\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. If every entry of $\text{args}$ and every value of $\mu$
has absolute value at most $W$, then the state whose location function lists the entries
of $\text{args}$ in order and is $0$ beyond the list, and whose memory function is
$\mu$, has all location and memory values bounded in absolute value by $W$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded state after a call frame]
\lean{Light.bounded_callFrame}
\label{Light.bounded_callFrame}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Expr, Light.Expr.Safe, Light.Expr.abs_val_le, Light.Expr.val, Light.State, Light.State.Bounded, Light.bounded_frame, Light.frame}
\difficulty{4}
Let a machine state have location and memory values in $\mathbb Z$, and let the word
bound be $W$. Suppose every location and memory value in a state $\sigma$ has absolute
value at most $W$. For a list of expressions that are safe in $\sigma$, form a new
location function by placing their values, in order, at the corresponding indices and
assigning $0$ at indices beyond the list; retain $\sigma$'s memory. The resulting state
has every location and memory value bounded in absolute value by $W$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of bounded states]
\lean{Light.Exec.bounded}
\label{Light.Exec.bounded}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Exec, Light.Expr.abs_val_le, Light.State, Light.State.Bounded, Light.Stmt, Light.abs_update_le, Light.bounded_callFrame}
\difficulty{5}
Let a statement execute under limits, program $P$, and depth $d$, from state $\sigma$ to
state $\sigma'$ with cost $c$. If every location and memory value in $\sigma$ has
absolute value at most the word limit, then every location and memory value in $\sigma'$
also has absolute value at most the word limit.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Memory outside the address range is unchanged]
\lean{Light.Exec.mem_outside}
\label{Light.Exec.mem_outside}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Exec, Light.State, Light.Stmt}
\difficulty{5}
Let a statement execute under limits, program $P$, and depth $d$, from state $\sigma$ to
state $\sigma'$ with cost $c$. For every natural-number address $a$ at least the space
limit, the memory value is unchanged:
$\sigma'.\operatorname{mem}(a)=\sigma.\operatorname{mem}(a)$.
\end{theorem}
